Alex.confusing: The Owl's wording "lay an egg in their nest" was unclear about whose nest gets the egg, and that dispute decided round 2's accusations. Drew and Ellis argued over it, and I couldn't tell who was right.
Alex.fun: Round 3's last-round all-in: I threw all seven cards at Ellis, banked 57 points, and that was the game-winning move.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn reports name who visited you and whose nest changed, so the Owl, Falcon and Tit egg rules are easier to check at the table.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I backed Blair's and Finley's read and threw my Wild at Drew, a Farm player, which cost the round. I'd have leaned on the egg-count contradictions more and kept my card unless the accusation was clearly proven.

Blair.confusing: The dawn reports were hard to read: an Owl's egg lands in the visited player's nest, but some players said it was their own, and Drew's "nobody visited me" was not clearly a lie until later. Role changes between rounds also made claims hard to trust.
Blair.fun: Round 1 went cleanly: the Owl and Falcon checks plus Casey's false Pigeon claim got the table to vote out the Sphinx, and Farm won.
Blair.change: Make dawn reports say explicitly who visited whom and which egg came from which visit, so players can't argue over the same +1.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I threw only my Wild, banking 0 points on a win, when I was confident about Casey; I should have thrown a high card like a 13 to bank real points. In round 2 I threw at Drew, a Farm player, instead of pressing Casey, the real Sphinx, which lost the round.

Casey.confusing: The dawn egg rules were unclear: whether an Owl's egg goes to the visited player or the Owl itself, and what a Pigeon visit does to the target's nest. Drew and Ellis argued about this for a whole day.
Casey.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: Ellis claimed a Pigeon visit that the nest counts contradicted, and the table turned on them in one day. Their final 7-card throw was a bold move.
Casey.change: I would make the score less lopsided, since Alex ended with 60 from banking one big throw while others sat near 10. A cap on banked value or a smaller bonus for a single winning throw would keep the game closer.
Casey.regret: In round 1, as the Sphinx, I named Turkey and visited Blair without a real lead, which wasted my one reveal. I should have named a role I suspected, such as Owl or Falcon, and visited the player I was least sure of.

Drew.confusing: The Owl's egg wording ("lay an egg in their nest") and the dawn report's visitor reporting were easy to misread, which led me to make a false "nobody visited me" claim in round 2.
Drew.fun: Round 1, when Finley's Tit claim and Blair's Owl visitor list exposed Casey's Pigeon story and the table got Casey eggsecuted.
Drew.change: Make dawn reports spell out exactly which visitors and egg changes each role can see, so players can't misread them.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I said "nobody visited me," which was an overreach from my Owl report; I would stick to what my report actually showed and not claim knowledge I didn't have.

Ellis.confusing: The Hawk and Owl egg rules were hard to read: I took my Round 2 egg as proof Drew was Meowfia, but it likely came from Casey's Pigeon visit, and I couldn't tell which claim was the real source. Whether an Owl gains an egg from its own target or from its own empty visit was also unclear.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 went cleanly: six players converged on Casey, the Sphinx, through the Owl and Tit egg cross-checks. Casey's Pigeon story collapsed under the table's questions.
Ellis.change: Publish each egg's source, or at least which visits caused each change, so players aren't guessing between overlapping claims like Pigeon and Hawk.
Ellis.regret: In Round 2 I pushed the vote on Drew from a single egg that was probably Casey's Pigeon egg, and Drew was Farm; I should have said the egg could have another source and held my throw. Had I done that, Farm may have kept the round.

Finley.confusing: The Kookaburra confusion rule was hard to track: my dawn report said I was confused but didn't say which parts were wrong, so I couldn't tell whether my Drew read was real.
Finley.fun: Round 3's day, where Blair, Casey, and Alex coordinated a vote on Ellis and Ellis's Pigeon claim fell apart in front of everyone.
